In [[mathematics]], specifically [[arithmetic geometry]], '''prismatic cohomology''' is a [[cohomology]] introduced by [[Bhargav Bhatt (mathematician)|Bhargav Bhatt]] and [[Peter Scholze]] for [[p-adic number|{{math|''p''}}-adic]] [[formal scheme]]s.{{sfnp|Bhatt|Scholze|2022}} It generalizes various {{math|''p''}}-adic cohomology theories.

Fix a [[prime number|prime]] <math>p</math>. A '''prism''' is a pair <math>(A,I)</math>, where <math>A</math> is a [[p-derivation|{{math|'' δ''}}-ring]] with <math>p</math>-derivation <math>\delta_A</math> and <math>I</math> is an ideal of <math>A</math> defining a [[Divisor (algebraic geometry)#Cartier divisor|Cartier divisor]] in <math>\operatorname{Spec}(A)</math>, such that <math>A</math> is derived <math>(p,I)</math>-adically complete and the ideal <math>I+\phi_A(I)A</math> contains <math>p</math>,{{sfnp|nLab}} where the associated map <math>\phi_A : A\to A</math> given by <math display="block">\phi_A(x) = x^p + p \delta_A(x)</math> is a [[ring homomorphism]], which then necessarily lifts the [[Frobenius endomorphism]] on <math>A/(p)</math>.{{sfnp|Bhatt|Scholze|2022|loc=remark 2.1}}
